solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fame from something other than talent

parts.note: a thing other than X is not X, giving the negative word NOT
a talent is a natural ability

explanation.surface: A cynical remark about celebrities who are famous without having any gift.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sneer at celebrities, and the wordplay literally says the same thing: fame that comes from a lack of talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Notability is the state of being widely known or eminent, a close synonym of renown.

clue.text: Pointless to get rid of posh bouquet

indicators.note: getting rid of something means taking those letters out

parts.note: something pointless is of no use, the phrase NO USE
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a fancy flower arrangement as a waste of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouquet here is the wine-taster's sense, the smell of a wine, not a bunch of flowers. 'to get rid of' removes U from NO USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's nose is its aroma, which tasters also call its bouquet.

clue.text: Warm weather Malaysia enjoys

indicators.note: enjoys says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A travel note that Malaysia has hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enjoys' is the containment signal: the word that holds the letters is said to enjoy (have) them.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal clothing keeps you warm, so the adjective is a synonym for warm or heat-retaining.

clue.text: Campaigners here having reasons to support development of tablet

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, supporting it
the development of the word tablet is its letters worked into a new shape

parts.note: grounds for something are reasons for it

explanation.surface: Political campaigners justify the launch of a new tablet computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' rearranges TABLET into BATTLE; 'to support' puts GROUNDS underneath it. The campaigners are military ones fighting a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Battlegrounds are the places where military campaigns are fought, so campaigning soldiers are found there.

clue.text: Shunning outsiders, block dumb introduction of some temporary workers

indicators.note: shunning the outsiders of each word leaves only its inner letters
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An employer wants to block the hiring of some stand-ins without explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shunning outsiders' applies to both block and dumb, giving LOC and UM; 'introduction of' gives S from some.
explanation.definitionFit: Locums are doctors or clergy who stand in for a regular holder of the post for a short spell.

clue.text: Bladed implement turns egg over

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: turns as a verb means spins
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget that flips an egg over in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SPINS plus NIT end to end, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin snips are heavy shears used to cut sheet metal, so they are a tool with blades.

clue.text: United lacking following? That's not new

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: things that are fused have been joined or united
F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A football fan grumbles that Manchester United have no supporters left, so the club is past it.
explanation.walkthrough: United is not the football club but the past participle meaning joined; 'lacking' removes F (following) from FUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used is second-hand, which is the opposite of brand new.

clue.text: Disturbing teen, such provocations could be untimeliest

indicators.note: disturbing the letters of teen alongside the answer mixes them together
could be says the combined letters may be rearranged into the given word

parts.note: the word is taken as written as the full letter pool
taken as written as the extra letters

explanation.surface: A teenager is being upset by things happening at the worst possible moment.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: the answer plus TEEN, mixed up ('Disturbing', 'could be'), makes UNTIMELIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that provoke a response, the plural of stimulus.

clue.text: When worker's let off for instruction from leader easy to misconstrue

definitions.text: When worker's let off for instruction

indicators.note: misconstruing words means getting them wrong, so their letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A boss's easy-going comment is open to being misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to misconstrue' rearranges the letters of LEADER EASY.
explanation.definitionFit: Day release is a British scheme letting employees leave work one day a week to attend college courses.

clue.text: Retracted muscles spasm, making one incredulous

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pecs is short for pectoral muscles
a tic is an involuntary muscle spasm

explanation.surface: A patient whose muscles twitch and pull back is told the cause and does not believe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retracted' signals the reversal: the muscles are drawn back, read right to left, before the spasm is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic is a doubter, a person who is inclined not to believe what they are told.

clue.text: Teased last in year in cruel manner

indicators.note: teased can mean combed out or untangled, so these letters are pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pupil was mocked for coming bottom in their year, and unkindly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teased' rearranges LAST IN into NASTIL, then Y is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting nastily means behaving in a spiteful, unkind way.

clue.text: Standing after drink? Ale not finished, it's presumed

indicators.note: after places the word for standing behind the drink in the answer

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
one's standing is one's position or rank

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter is left off

explanation.surface: Someone stands up after a drink, assuming their pint is still there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link word. Sup is a slightly old-fashioned British word for drinking, often used of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppositional describes something based on supposition, that is assumed rather than proven.

clue.text: Madame grabbing a French article, with no hesitation changes in Gents

indicators.note: grabbing means holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: Mme is the written abbreviation of the French title Madame
le is the French masculine definite article
a pause is a brief hesitation

explanation.surface: A French lady storms into the men's toilets, and the changes made there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' and 'no' are used as written. Gents (British for a men's public lavatory) misleads: it means men in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The so-called male menopause is the set of physical and emotional changes some men go through in middle age.

clue.text: Sad fine comedian failed

parts.note: feeling down means feeling sad
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
Woody Allen is the comedian and film-maker

explanation.surface: A comic did badly at the gig and feels miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: Comedian stands for a specific one, Woody Allen.
explanation.definitionFit: Downfallen is a rare word for ruined, brought down from a high position, so it describes someone who has come to grief.

clue.text: Help old boy cross, road's beginning to heave

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: to heave out is to throw away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a liger is a cross between a lion and a tigress

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A request to help an elderly man cross the road and lift him over.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross is a noun, a hybrid animal: LIGER. 'to heave' throws out R, the first letter ('beginning') of road's, leaving LIGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to do them a favour, that is to assist them.

clue.text: Pertinent quartet of tech terms, in short

parts.note: four abbreviated technology terms, shortened as 'in short' says; the first is APP, short for application
the second tech term: OS is short for operating system
the third tech term: IT is short for information technology
the fourth tech term: E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Someone praises a pithy summary of four technical expressions as right on the money.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as APP, OS, IT and E, four abbreviations from computing and technology; 'in short' says they are shortened forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite remarks are well suited to the occasion, which is to say relevant.

clue.text: Extremely dubious book turned up in lounge

indicators.note: in places the reversed book inside the word for lounge

parts.note: to lounge is to rest idly

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A doubtful book has appeared in someone's sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns TOME into EMOT, which goes 'in' REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Remotest is the superlative of remote, as in the remotest chance: the most unlikely, hence most doubtful.

clue.text: Watt in exhibition centre by sign: 'Steam Engine Inventor'

indicators.note: by means next to, so the sign follows
in puts the unit's symbol inside the exhibition centre's letters

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham
W is the symbol for the watt, the unit of power
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: James Watt appears at an exhibition beside a placard naming a steam-engine pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: Watt suggests the engineer James Watt but is the unit W. The NEC is the National Exhibition Centre, a large venue near Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Newcomen built the first practical steam engine in 1712, decades before Watt improved on it.

clue.text: Bats desire birds to leave lake

parts.note: will is desire or wish

indicators.note: to leave means one letter departs from the word

parts.note: owls are birds
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Bats would like the birds to clear off from the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats are not the flying animals but cricket bats; 'to leave' takes L from OWLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are traditionally made from willow wood, so willows can stand for the bats themselves.

clue.text: Subjects of European city

definitions.meaning: vassals owing allegiance to a feudal lord
belonging to the Belgian city of Liège, its possessive form

explanation.surface: A query about the people of a city on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a vassal bound to a lord, and Liège is a city in Belgium, so its possessive reads the same.

clue.text: Exits, self-conscious dropping head with diminished bearing

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the trimmed bearing is placed next to the moved word
in a down clue the head letter drops to the bottom of the word

parts.note: the ego is the conscious self

indicators.note: diminished means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: south is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A shy person leaves a room with their head down and shoulders slumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping head' moves the E of EGO to the end, giving GOE; 'diminished' cuts SOUTH to SOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Goes out means leaves or departs, so it matches exits as a verb in the third person.

clue.text: Bills increased when housing daughter — makes sense

indicators.note: housing means holding inside

parts.note: bills are posters or advertisements, ads
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
up means increased, as in prices are up

explanation.surface: Household bills went up once the daughter moved back home, which is no surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Bills are not invoices but advertisements, ADS, which go 'housing' D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that adds up is logical and consistent, so it is coherent and believable.

clue.text: Exhausted G&T? Be patient

parts.note: all in is informal for worn out
G is the abbreviation for good and T for time, so the pair expands to those two words

explanation.surface: Someone who has finished the gin and tonic is told to wait for a refill.
explanation.walkthrough: G&T looks like gin and tonic but is read as G and T expanded into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase all in good time is said to someone in a hurry, urging them to wait.

clue.text: You'd get wound taking this rifle into bed

indicators.note: you'd get introduces the result of the operation the clue describes
this refers to the answer, which is to be placed somewhere
into says where the answer goes, inside the word for bed

parts.note: wound in the sense of twisted together, braided
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier is hurt by taking a gun to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put the answer into BED and you get BRAIDED, wound in the twisted sense, so the answer is BRAIDED less B and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack it, much as a raid plunders it.

clue.text: Butcher's fine feeding stray from back of store

indicators.note: feeding means going into the other word

parts.note: to stray from a path is to lose it
OK means fine

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A butcher's fine meat, fed to a stray dog from the back of the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook = look. 'stray from' means lose, as in losing your way.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's and a look-see are both informal words for a quick look.

clue.text: Ragged horse carrying knight and a lady overseas

indicators.note: carrying means holding the other letter within
ragged means torn and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A scruffy horse carries a knight and his lady to foreign lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ragged' gives SEHOR from HORSE, which goes 'carrying' N, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: Senhora is the Portuguese title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs or madam abroad.

clue.text: Make home clean, scrubbing house

indicators.note: scrubbing means wiping out, so letters are removed

parts.note: clean in the sense of honest, above board

explanation.surface: House-proud advice to make your home spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: Clean is the moral sense, HONEST, and 'scrubbing' removes HO from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To nest is to settle in and build a home, as birds do.

clue.text: Put details in specified order?

indicators.note: in together with the later word order says the letters are arranged into a fresh sequence
order completes the phrase in order, putting the letters into a new sequence

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange the details in a set sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... order' splits around the definition; PUT DETAILS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipulated terms are ones laid down or specified as a condition of an agreement.
